## Purpose

The Alembic revision chain for the backend's SQLAlchemy schema — a single linear history from an
empty database to the current head (`0030`).

Every deployment and every local `alembic upgrade head` depends on it; no other module writes
DDL.

## Shape

One file per revision, hand-numbered `0001`-`0030` (`0003` is absent — never cut) with an
explicit `down_revision` chain, so the chain stays single-head and `alembic upgrade head` is
deterministic.

- [0001_initial_schema.py](../../backend/alembic/versions/0001_initial_schema.py) — baseline: `users`, `chat_sessions`, `messages`, `workflow_runs`,
  `revoked_tokens`.
- `0002`-`0009` — small additive columns/tables (handoff credentials, token usage, user
  tier/admin/preferred-model, workflow model id) plus a `0009` no-op that documents a
  schema-debt audit and re-anchors the chain.
- `0010`-`0015` — the Phase 3/5 Artifact_Store era: `workflow_artifacts` (thin store) lands in
  `0010`, workflow tables (`workflow_clarifications`, `workflow_memory`, `workflows`) in `0011`,
  `workflow_runs` grows its execution-gate/session columns in `0012`, `pipeline_run_id` collapses
  into `id` in `0013`. `0014` adds the durable typed-artifact schema (`artifact_refs`,
  `workspaces`, `run_events`, `run_capabilities`) and backfills a default workspace per existing
  run. `0015` is the **one deliberately destructive migration**: it drops the now-orphaned thin
  `workflow_artifacts` table once every reader moved onto `artifact_refs`.
- `0016`-`0020` — capability-hardening / multi-agent era: `validation_results`, `gate_events`,
  `hook_runs` (`0016`); `repositories` + `mcp_credentials` (`0017`, Phase 9 repo workflows);
  `exec_runs` audit table (`0018`, Phase 10 sandbox exec); `subagent_runs` (`0019`, Phase 11
  fan-out); `wave_runs` (`0020`, Phase 12 wave scheduler).
- `0021`-`0027` — product-feature columns: saved user workflows reusing the dormant `workflows`
  table (`0021`), deliverable mimetype/filename (`0022`), launch-time `selections_json` (`0023`),
  `run_events` uniqueness backstops (`0024`), `deep_link_nonces` (`0025`), per-child task identity
  on `subagent_runs` for crash resume (`0026`), OpenDesign `od_context_json` for resumed
  od_ppt/prototype runs (`0027`).
- `0028`-`0030` — repair and index tail: `0028` idempotently repairs 0024/0025 drift on a
  database that was stamped past them without the DDL ever applying; `0029` reconciles duplicate
  `run_events` rows produced by the seq-allocation race before enforcing the uniqueness
  constraint 0028 deferred; `0030` adds a `(user_id, created_at)` index for history-list queries.
  **Current head: `0030`.**

## Why this shape

Every migration after the `0009` audit declares itself additive-only (create table / add
nullable column) and states that discipline in its own docstring — **the only sanctioned
non-additive migration is `0015`'s drop of the dead thin artifact store**, and it is called out
explicitly as the exception.

New tables consistently carry `owner_id` + `workspace_id` (not null) so the `ScopedStore`
default-deny read filter covers them from creation, and status/kind/provider columns are free
`String`, never `sa.Enum`, so adding a new value never needs a migration.

`0028`/`0029` exist because a stamped-but-unapplied revision is a real failure mode in this
history — they are worked examples of detecting and repairing that drift without a destructive
re-stamp.

Not attempted here: no down-migration squashing, no consolidated baseline — **the full chain is
kept** so `alembic downgrade` stays meaningful at any point in history.
